_doc: Words the player reads. Rule: one or two short sentences per line, a speaker on every line, nothing longer than a breath. Lore notes are optional reading.
intro: Three hundred years ago, the sun went out.
Tallow lives under the last Great Lantern. Tonight, for seven heartbeats, it went dark.
Something came over the wall in those seven heartbeats. It took a child.
You are the Ninth Lamplighter. The other eight are dead or missing. Go.

captions.first_dark: Outside your light, the Dusk hits harder. Keep it fed.
captions.first_level: The lantern burns brighter for you. Spend your points (K, P).
captions.lamp_lit: The waylamp holds. This ground remembers the light.
captions.relight_start: Hold the lamp until it catches. The dark will come for it.
captions.act_end: End of Act 1. The moths are gone from the road. The Dusk is remembering.

teague_cairn.title: A note under a cold lantern
lines: If you're reading this, Ottilie sent you. She lies when she's frightened.
Ask her what the Great Lantern burns. Watch her hands when she answers.
— T. Morrow, Eighth

brennick.title: Old Brennick, still fishing
lines: A woodcutter, turned to glass where he sat. His line still hangs in the water.
Tied to the rod, a child's note: 'Da. I bring you tea on Tuesdays. Come home when the fish bite.'

order_rules.title: A page from a Lamplighter's cache
lines: Rule one: never look into the shard.
Rule two: it is not a stone.
Rule three: if it speaks, it is dreaming. Do not answer.

teague_road.title: A note in the roadside shrine
lines: The road lamps aren't failing. Something drinks them.
The moths carry the light east, into the hills. Like bees. Like offerings.

teague_hollow.title: Teague's last camp
lines: Followed the moths down. They feed her. She feeds on what the sun dreams.
It is remembering, Ottilie. The Dusk is remembering.

river_note.title: A note on the river shrine
lines: The water goes up because something up there is thirsty.
Not the sky. The sky is just the way.

lull_bell.title: An inscription on the bell's lectern
lines: CAST FOR THE ORDER OF THE LAMP. YEAR ONE.
TO BE RUNG ONLY AT NOON.
(Below, scratched by a newer hand: 'It worked. Forgive us. It worked.')

falls_note.title: A soaked page by a cold campfire
lines: Climbed the falls. The water goes up and so does the noise — a bell, far off.
Lights in the marsh ahead. Most of them have teeth.

marsh_note.title: The order's marsh shrine
lines: THE BELL ROAD. KEEP TO THE STONES.
WE CARRIED IT HERE SO NO ONE IN THE CITIES WOULD HEAR IT RING.
(Scratched under it: 'They still hear it. In their sleep.')

ford_note.title: A shrine on the ford road
lines: Hollin's Ford was the last town to see the sun.
It saw it go down at four o'clock on a Tuesday. It decided not to let go of that.

school_note.title: A child's slate by the schoolhouse door
lines: WHAT HAPPENED ON TUESDAY
The sun was too hot for a year. The lamp people rang a bell. The sun went to sleep. We were so glad.
(The same words, in the same hand, scratched over each other until the slate is white.)

signs.road: The Ember Road  -  Tallow west, the hills east
signs.east: East: the Ember Road  -  (scratched under it: the lamps are out)
signs.north: North: the River Road  -  (the river is not where it used to be)
signs.river: The Upward River  -  Ferry at the hamlet
signs.marsh: North: the Saltmarsh  -  keep to the road
signs.ford: Hollin's Ford  -  Tallow west  -  (every clock: four)
